database_note: The collisions table records traffic collision events, while parties and victims describe the individuals involved. Use case_ids as a lookup index for the processing year. To connect these tables, join collisions to parties using the case_id column. Note that parties stores case_id as a DOUBLE, which may cause precision loss when joining with the integer case_id in collisions. Similarly, join parties to victims using both case_id and party_number. Do not rely on the id column in victims as a unique key, as duplicates exist across cases. This structure allows you to link specific collision details to the drivers, pedestrians, or cyclists involved, and further to their injury outcomes.
database_fact: The collisions table records traffic collision events, while parties and victims describe the individuals involved. The parties table stores case_id as a DOUBLE. The victims table contains duplicates across cases. The tables connect by joining collisions to parties using the case_id column, and joining parties to victims using both case_id and party_number.
